scope: The twelve test files explicitly delegated by root; full source reading only, no test execution or fresh application audit. Findings below are coverage/contract notes on already-existing audit2 findings, not new defects.

observations.topic: MM-01 is supported by an older explicit cookie-cleanup expectation
observations.assessment: Readiness tests explicitly require deletion Set-Cookie on401, including a session revoked during pending SMTP verification. They send raw Cookie headers, inspect responses individually and do not install a replacement session in a native shared cookie jar before the old401 arrives. These green assertions validate the old cleanup policy and cannot disprove the delayed-response race already identified in MM-01. This is a scope/contract observation for the existing finding; the current readiness source was not newly reproduced here.
observations.futureFocusedRegression: If protected-route cleanup policy changes in the MM-01 fix, audit and adjust these explicit expectations deliberately. A composed delayed old401/new login/browser-cookie-jar test should retain the newer cookie. No rerun or change authorized by this reading.

observations.topic: SMTP readiness intentionally excludes mail delivery and expiry claims
observations.assessment: The readiness transport only verifies authentication; sendMail/sendVerification/sendPasswordReset are forbidden and outbox counts remain0. Consequently neither successful SMTP readiness nor this native SQL integration tests claim+lock-time advancement+real mail worker. They cannot contradict DOM-01 or establish reception of mail. Retain their no-email contract.

observations.topic: Readiness has relevant concurrency/clock guards but these do not qualify other components
observations.assessment: Readiness explicitly reserves its busy slot while async quota/session proof/factory work waits, rechecks revoked/expired session after awaited budgets, sanitizes invalid late clocks and closes late transports. This is useful positive coverage for readiness and a pattern for a future focused witness admission fix; it is not an integration test of witness transfers or access renewal result checking.

observations.topic: Current route failure and access renewal composition remain outside this test set
observations.assessment: Entry tests validate fixed role destinations, stale fetch generations, hidden/BFCache state, explicit install and choice semantics. They do not load manual-backups.html or follow its header link, nor call the access renewal service composed with a fresh-clock store. No contradictory assertion or regression proof for FI-PWA-01/AUTH-DATA-01 was found here.

observations.topic: Managed runtime protects the old forced-stop boundary and the video/witness mode separation
observations.assessment: Tests distinguish graceful, forced SIGKILL and nonzero drain, preserve rejected stop/destroy promises and verify the actual shim no-orphan/listener boundary using synthetic children. They reject video without managed closures and reject video+parentGateway combinations. This supports the optional witness exposure boundary; it neither exercises the witness body-admission race nor requires a real backup/restore/PC operation.

observations.topic: Release tests verify startup observation, not independent deployed identity or feature integration
observations.assessment: Release tests use a temporary Git checkout, dirty/untracked cases, bounded metadata and a frozen startup snapshot emitted by a synthetic listening application. These checks prevent expected-version fabrication but do not prove the actual remote PID/checkout or latest delivery. The short feature test checks technical1.7.2 versus other product versions for two booleans only; it is not video writer/backup integration or a comprehensive future release-version policy.

Both integrations explicitly require disposable loopback databases and default33-migration non-video schema. This is consistent with loadMigrations() profile selection, not evidence that active video schema36 is stale. They are skipped unless an explicit DB opt-in is present; no qualification success is inferred here. entry-lifecycle was already covered by frontend_identity_pwa and is listed once as overlap, not a second unique test.

observations.topic: DOM-01 expired mail claim integration gap
observations.assessment: The lifecycle fixtures replace the mail store, keep clock frozen, and return jobs with no expiry or lease-until metadata. They exercise stop/drain/refund ordering, not SQL lock time advancing before SMTP. Green outcomes cannot cover the existing DOM-01 finding. If a future fix adds an expiry-based worker guard, update the synthetic job contract deliberately while preserving the no-SMTP-after-stop and no-refund-after-SMTP assertions.

observations.topic: DOM-01 impact contracted by telemetry tests
observations.assessment: Partial failed batches make readiness unavailable; a later successful empty loop restores it. A sent-but-unacknowledged expired-lease attempt should therefore not be called a permanent service failure or proof of no SMTP acceptance. These tests do not conceal link expiry; they specify bounded aggregate telemetry and recovery.

observations.topic: Operational SQL integration is sampling only
observations.assessment: Real MariaDB tests create queue rows, compare them before/after read-only samples, enforce runtime DML privilege separation, then configure an auth-only server with all delivery features disabled and mailWorker:null. They do not compose actual delivery worker+claim+clock or cover renewal, witness, chat cookie races. This is a scope limit, not a new defect.

observations.topic: Readiness is cached process health, not functional certification
observations.assessment: The tests intentionally require no SQL/private handler on public readiness GET, coalesce samples, reject timed-out late success, use monotonic age and drain the real outstanding query. Their green readiness result certifies recent sampling and completed worker loops only; it cannot contradict any current functional finding or establish successful user delivery.

observations.topic: Snapshot microseconds and bounded counts are explicit contracts
observations.assessment: Counts cap at1000 with an independent truncation bit, scheduling instants preserve SQL microsecond ordering, only aggregate fields are queried, and notification sampling is opt-in. No expectation here requires unbounded scans or changes the current capacity conclusions.

observations.topic: The 33-migration integration fixture is an intentional profile boundary
observations.assessment: The test calls default loadMigrations() and asserts33 for its non-video disposable database; it is not a failed claim that the active video schema has only33. This does not independently qualify video/push integration. Do not manufacture a version finding from that assertion.

observations.topic: Current findings outside these five tests
observations.assessment: AUTH-DATA-01 (renewal composition), BH-01 (witness admission), MM-01 (delayed401 cookie) and FI-PWA-01 (backup link) are not exercised by these test paths. No contradictory expectations or regression proof for those defects was found in these files.

coverageAccounting.rootPreviouslyReadPortions: Root had read readiness portions; these entries record completion of their full read, not an independent extra source count. migrations.test.mjs is not claimed in this report.

limits: No test, CI, HTTP fixture, SQL, child process, browser or other code executed by either reviewer.
Reading assertions documents expected behavior and blind spots; it does not create evidence that currently unrun assertions pass or fail.
No new source defect, production incident, backup/restore/PC task or security conclusion invented from missing tests.
No repository file or existing evidence modified; output reports only.
